Workshop Experience

During the workshop, I got practical exposure to real-world problem solving. Instead of only learning theory, we visited the server/work area, observed real problems, discussed possible causes, and worked together to find practical solutions.

The workshop helped me understand how technology and practical thinking can be used to identify problems, analyze them and develop useful solutions.

1

We tested the prototype, observed its working, identified improvements and refined the design.

Lemon Size Grader — My Innovation Project

The Lemon Size Grader is a simple, low-cost and practical device designed to separate lemons according to their size. The idea focuses on making the grading process easier and more efficient using a simple mechanical design.

PROBLEM

Manual lemon size sorting can take time and requires continuous human effort. Different-sized lemons need to be separated for better handling and grading.

OUR IDEA

We designed a simple Lemon Size Grader using a low-cost mechanical approach. The design allows lemons to move through different grading sections so that they can be separated according to size.

WHAT WE FOCUSED ON
Low-cost constructionSimple working mechanismEasy operationPractical village/farm useEasy maintenanceManual operationSize-based lemon separation

Lemon Grader PhotosReal photographs of the prototype

How It Works

🍋

1. Input

Put the lemons into the starting/inlet section.

⚙️

2. Movement

The lemons move through the grading mechanism.

📏

3. Separation

Different sizes are separated through different grading sections.

📦

4. Collection

Collect the lemons from their respective size/grade sections.

Advantages

💰 Low Cost

🧩 Simple Design

🖐️ Easy to Operate

⏱️ Saves Manual Sorting Effort

🌾 Useful for Small Farmers

🔧 Easy Maintenance

🎒 Practical and Portable

🌿 Environment-Friendly Mechanical Approach

Challenges & LimitationsHonest notes for future improvement

Manual operation is required.

Sorting accuracy depends on the design and size difference.

Very irregularly shaped lemons may not always separate perfectly.

The prototype may require further testing and improvement.
